## Research Lead: F2Agent — Modality-Aware Adaptive Fusion for Multi-Agent Trading (arXiv:2608.05668, flagged 2026-08-19)

**Source:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05668 (submitted 2026-08-06). Detail gathered via WebSearch at abstract level only; the 32-page paper itself has not been fetched/read in full, so treat specifics below as abstract-reported, not independently verified against full text.

**What it is:** A hierarchy of specialized agents (Market Analysis, Technical Analysis, News Analysis, Sentiment Analysis) feeding into a **Modality-aware Adaptive Fusion Mechanism** plus **Noise-robust Consistency Regularization**, evaluated with an end-to-end backtesting engine on six stocks and cryptocurrency assets against 16 baselines.

**How this differs from what's already in this page:** TradingAgents, HedgeAgents, and the CGX entry above (2026-08-18) are all fundamentally about **debate/consensus** — multiple agents argue a position and a mechanism (majority vote, Meta-Evaluator gate, embedding-similarity filter) resolves disagreement into a single decision or abstention. F2Agent instead targets **input fusion** — how to weight and combine four different *modalities* of agent output (not four opinions on the same modality) when one input channel (e.g. News) is noisier or less reliable than another at a given moment. This is closer to a sensor-fusion problem than a debate problem: the "Adaptive" part reportedly reweights modality contributions dynamically rather than treating all four analyst agents as equally trustworthy inputs at all times.

**Reported results (abstract-level, unverified):** ">20% relative improvement in annualized return on average" vs. 16 competitive baselines, with headline per-asset returns as high as 120.48% (GOOG) and 148.41% (TSLA) cited in search-result summaries. These numbers were not independently checked against the paper's methodology section (cost model, OOS window, survivorship handling) and should be treated with the same skepticism this wiki applies to all headline multi-agent-trading claims per the Agentic Trading Survey 2026 finding already logged above ("reproducibility crisis: 0/19 papers fully reproducible," "transaction costs absent in 63%") -- no reason yet to believe F2Agent is an exception, and it has not been run through the [Shared Evaluation Checklist](../shared-eval-checklist.md) or [LLM Alpha Validation Checklist](llm-alpha-validation.md).

**Relevance / possible future direction (not staged as a hypothesis tonight):** If a future PEAD or momentum hypothesis wants to blend multiple signal modalities (e.g. H174's FinBERT text score + a technical momentum score + a macro regime gate) rather than picking one dominant filter, F2Agent's adaptive-fusion framing is a candidate design reference distinct from anything currently cited in [Attention Mechanisms and Vector Quantization](attention-cross-sectional-factor-models.md) or [E2E Portfolio Policies](e2e-portfolio-policies.md), both of which are single-modality (price/factor) architectures. No hypothesis number assigned; logged as a design reference only, same treatment as the 2026-08-18 CGX entry above.

**Cross-references:** [CGX — Consensus-Gated Execution], [Agentic Trading Survey 2026](../../ai-industry/agentic-trading-survey-2026.md), [Shared Evaluation Checklist](../shared-eval-checklist.md)
